content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm looking for assistance with a straightforward issue. My goal is for when input I1 turns ON, merker M1 activates for a set duration, then after that time ends, M1 switches OFF and M2 activates for another set period, and so on through M10. Once M10 activates, it should remain ON as long as I1 is ON. At any point, if I1 turns OFF, all merkers should switch OFF. I appreciate any help or advice.
Here's a possible solution. Note that M8 isn't used in this scenario because, in [product_name], it has a special function—on every first program cycle, M8 outputs a signal of 1.

Thanks a lot! And yes, M8 is a unique case. My reason for setting up this sequence is because my program currently operates with a certain logic and timing. However, the customer now needs the program to run with new timing parameters every 24 hours. So when M1 is ON, it uses the first timer set, when M2 is ON, the second set is used, and so on. On the last day, the final set of parameters runs indefinitely. I hope this method allows the customer to use pre-set 'recipes' for multiple days, avoiding daily changes to timing parameters.
